source_evidence: Stock funds invest primarily in stocks or equities. A stock is an instrument that represents an ownership interest (called equity) in a company and a proportional share in the company’s assets and profits.
answer: Stock and bond ETFs differ mainly in what they hold. Stock funds invest primarily in company stocks, which represent ownership interests in those companies. Their value can rise or fall quickly, and performance depends in part on how the underlying companies do. Bond funds invest primarily in bonds or other debt securities. The bonds they hold can vary in risk, return, duration, and volatility, so bond funds do not all behave alike.
